body:
Shift-end items of the `domain:spec` seat, shift 2026-09-05T01:44Z → 2026-09-06T01:19Z (`session_01M59rPZZFzqhfMUPFqqZTkf`, `os-project-manager`), filed as one `finding` for the skills seat — the three collected categories only, ⛔ no advice list. Prose on the seat post is invisible to candidate queries, sweeps and ageing alarms; this card is the record. Reader: the skills seat's own finding triage.

## 1 · Platform facts (→ `references/platform-readings.md`, one line each)

- **Actions job logs**: `mcp__github__get_job_logs` returns the log body where REST `GET /actions/jobs/ID/logs` (a 302 to the blob host) is refused by the egress proxy. Used 2026-09-05 to read the merge-driver failure on PR #15973's head.
- **Corepack in CI**: `.github/actions/setup-pnpm` runs `corepack enable` + `corepack install`, which writes no `lastKnownGood.json`; a directory whose `package.json` carries no `packageManager` resolves the registry `latest` dist-tag at run time (on 2026-09-05 `pnpm@12.3.4`, whose CLI rejects `-s`, exit 2). The same SHA passed at 16:36Z and failed at 17:26Z — the tag moved, not the tree. A fixture `package.json` written by a self-test must carry the root manifest's `packageManager` (PR #16002); `COREPACK_DEFAULT_TO_LATEST=0` alone does not repair a store that already recorded 12.x (measured).
- **Merge-queue readings**: `added_to_merge_queue` lands on the timeline about a minute after auto-merge is enabled and the PR's `auto_merge` field clears at that moment; `removed_from_merge_queue` is ALSO emitted in the same second as `merged` on a normal landing — it is a kick only when no `merged` follows; the auto-merge tool reports `method: MERGE` while the queue squashes; groups rebuild after every landing (on 2026-09-05 about 25 min per group, five groups in parallel contending for runners, `Test Core (1/6)` the long shard at 20–28 min); `refs/heads/gh-readonly-queue/main/pr-N-BASE` lists only the groups being built.
- **Landing probes**: a literal-count probe (`git grep -c "passthrough()"`) counted the rewritten comments and read 6 on a tree where the code form was gone (#15469's landing); the probe must name a code form (`).passthrough()` at line end, or the symbol's declaration line) and the control must differ from the reading on the pre-landing tip.
- **Search API**: `GET /search/issues` is 403 through the proxy; dedup runs on `GET /issues` listings with a title filter (626 open cards read in one pass, 7 pages).
- **Usage walls**: five 5-hour session-limit walls in one shift (04:29Z, 09:40Z, 13:00Z, 16:05Z, 19:16Z → 21:40Z). Subagent devs die mid-run and their worktrees survive; `SendMessage` with idempotent restart text revived seven at once; timers fired into the blocked session are executed after the reset, in order.
- **Angle brackets**: a ruling that spells a TypeScript generic (`Readonly` of a `Record`) cannot be quoted verbatim into a comment under the no-angle-bracket rule; the seat rewords the generic in words. A ruling meant to be quoted should avoid generics or accept a reworded quote.

## 2 · Principle gaps (→ skills seat, ADR-class)

- **Dispatch template vs AGENTS.md:400**: the seat's dispatch template carried "post your own dev claim comment per the os-dev definition"; AGENTS.md says a dispatched executor inherits the seat's `Claim:` and posts no second claim. Two devs (#14892, #15710) followed AGENTS.md and flagged the conflict; the line left this seat's template at 15:58Z. The skill text should carry the AGENTS.md reading so the next seat does not re-derive it.
- **Rulings must not ask for a card id inside `.describe()` prose**: the doc-authoring gate refuses internal issue-id references there (measured on #14993 — the dev placed the id in an adjacent comment and the seat ruled it right). Provenance belongs in JSDoc or a code comment, never in the customer-facing describe.
- **A dispatch order that paraphrases the code's behaviour is a claim to be measured**: this seat's gloss on #15710 ("the fresh store's new row carries `verified_at: null`") was wrong against `attestFreshDatastore`, which writes one uniform attestation shape; the dev measured and contradicted it. Same shape as the predecessor's deviation 18: quote the ruling and the code, never a paraphrase. Three dev corrections of the seat this shift (#14892 fixture evidence, #15710 gloss, #14848's "the ruling's illustrative key names are not real keys") — all right; the «measure it and contradict me» line in every dispatch is the control that catches them.
- **Anchor-card discipline needs a re-scan step**: #15992 was filed 2 min after #15990 for the same failing check (main red) without a second listing read; the convention's "first filer wins" only works if the filer re-scans immediately before filing. Recorded on all three cards.
- **A cross-lane claim while the lane seat is seated**: #14935 (`domain:spec`) was claimed 19:08Z by `session_01ARYe3yQTQCUFm5qPYNgKaJ` (the cli seat's session) during this seat's usage wall, without setting the assignee; the card sits `pm:dispatched` with no assignee — invisible to the presence bit, visible only in the comments. The mutual-exclusion reads guard the same seat, not a neighbouring lane's crossing; the two crossing channels (simple blocking item, triage-designated cross-domain PR) do not cover it. Not undone — its PR #16029 is in the queue, contract review passed 22:28Z — but the successor must read that card's comments, not its assignee.
- **Seat-side gloss on JSON Schema**: a `.refine` on a typed string arm is unrepresentable in JSON Schema — the arm reads `{ type: 'string' }` where the parse refuses blank (#15028, the #15810 trade). Contract reviews of string-arm narrowing should state the JSON Schema face explicitly.

## 3 · Mechanizable (→ gate / script cards, ⛔ not prose)

- **os-dev step ① is vacuous off `packages/spec/src`**: the "build spec" step passes without measuring anything when the change is test-only or outside the package; the step should be conditioned on the file surface, or replaced by the dispatch-gates derivation that already lists the commands the diff needs.
- **Playbook walk radius costs a full turbo build**: the spec-property-retirement playbook's consumer walk (rule #15566) rebuilt the dependency closure per walk on #15513 (about 6 min per lap on a shared box); an affected-scoped walk (`turbo ls --affected` against the merge-base) would cut it without losing coverage.
- **Landing-watch probe template**: the timer text template should carry a code-form probe with a non-zero control by construction (see the platform fact above), so a mis-designed literal probe cannot be armed.
